newsitem.title: USA: Angeion sees stable role in device market.
newsitem.headline: Angeion sees stable role in device market.

text.p: Angeion Corp said Wednesday that its position in the medical device industry will not be changed by the proposed acquisition of Ventritex Inc by St. Jude Medical Inc.

"The company's goal has always been to be a self-sustaining company," said chairman and chief executive Whitney McFarlin, in a statement issued by the company. "This merger does not change Angeion's position in the industry."

St. Jude agreed to buy Ventritex in a stock swap valued at $505 million. Ventritex makes implantable defibrillators -- electronic devices implanted in the chest and connected to the heart to keep it from beating too rapidly.
Under a distribution agreement, St. Jude has been expected to soon begin selling Angeion's implantable defibrillator under St. Jude's Pacesetter label.
"Initially this may put greater emphasis on our own distribution network and direct sales force, which we have been developing during the last 12 months," McFarlin said.
McFarlin said the St. Jude Pacesetter distribution was intended to help Angeion launch its products.
"Our plan has always included phasing out OEM (orginal equipment manufacturer) sales in fiscal 1998. As these events unfold, we will be continuously evaluating our position," McFarlin said.

"This is the first consolidation to take place in the defibrillator industry and will probably not be the last ... We believe this merger may give Angeion a flexibility which we previously did not enjoy," McFarlin said.
